title.narrative: Strengthen the capacity of tripartite partners in developing and adopting a National Employment Policy (NES)

description.narrative:
Jamaica, with a population of approximately 2.8 million, is classified as an upper-middle-income country by the World Bank. Despite a rebound in GDP to pre-COVID levels and a record low unemployment rate of 4.5% in April 2023, economic growth remains low, averaging around 1% over the last three decades. The country faces challenges such as high informality rates (53.1%) and significant gender disparities in the labor market. Structural barriers in accessing credit and finance constrain entrepreneurship and private sector expansion, impacting productivity and job creation.
To address these issues, the Council of Ministries decided in late 2022 to develop a National Employment Policy, focusing on the blue economy and agriculture sectors. The policy process, led by the Office of the Prime Minister, involves the ILO's assistance in designing a NEP policy. The formulation will include a sensitisation workshop, comprehensive diagnostic analysis, and consultative social dialogue to ensure active engagement from all stakeholders. This initiative aims to enhance human capital quality and promote inclusive employment opportunities in Jamaica.
